'''David H. Douglass''' (born 1932) is an [[Americans|American]] [[physicist]] at the [[University of Rochester]].

== Background ==

{{Empty section|date=December 2022}}

==Climate change ==

A 2005 study by Douglass and fellow University of Rochester physicist Robert S. Knox argued that [[global climate model]]s underestimated the climate response to the [[Mount Pinatubo#1991 eruption|1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo]]. The study also contended that global temperature returned to normal much faster after the eruption than the models had predicted.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Douglass |first1=David H. |last2=Knox |first2=Robert S.|title=Climate forcing by the volcanic eruption of Mount Pinatubo|journal=Geophysical Research Letters|date=2005|volume=32|issue=5|pages=L05710 |doi=10.1029/2004GL022119|arxiv = physics/0509166 |bibcode = 2005GeoRL..32.5710D |s2cid=13563394 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Press release: AGU Journal highlights - 23 March 2005|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2005-03/agu-ajh032305.php|publisher=AGU via EurekAlert!|language=en|date=23 March 2005}}</ref>

A 2007 paper by Douglass and coworkers questioned the reliability of 22 of the most commonly used global climate models analyzed by [[Benjamin D. Santer]] and used by the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change|IPCC]] to predict accelerated warming in the [[troposphere]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Douglass|first=David H.|author2=Christy, John R. |author3=Pearson, Benjamin D. |author4= Singer, S. Fred |title=A comparison of tropical temperature trends with model predictions|journal=International Journal of Climatology|date=15 November 2008|volume=28|issue=13|pages=1693–1701|doi=10.1002/joc.1651|bibcode = 2008IJCli..28.1693D |s2cid=10364112 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Pearce">{{cite book |first=Fred |last=Pearce |authorlink=Fred Pearce |title=The Climate Files: The Battle for the Truth about Global Warming |date=2010 |publisher=[[Guardian Books]] |isbn=978-0-85265-229-9 |page=XIV}}</ref> The study had originally been submitted to ''[[Geophysical Research Letters]]'' the previous year, but was rejected in September 2006 on Santer's recommendation.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2010/feb/09/ipcc-report-author-data-openness | title=Victory for openness as IPCC climate scientist opens up lab doors | work=[[The Guardian]] | date=9 February 2010 | accessdate=15 March 2014 | last=Pearce |first=Fred}}</ref> Santer and 17 co-authors later rebutted Douglass' paper.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/joc.1756 | volume=28 | issue=13 | title=Consistency of modelled and observed temperature trends in the tropical troposphere | year=2008 | journal=International Journal of Climatology | pages=1703–1722 | last1 = Santer | first1 = B. D.| bibcode=2008IJCli..28.1703S | s2cid=14941858 | url=http://eprints.maynoothuniversity.ie/6558/1/PT_consistency%202008.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Heffernan|first=Olive|title=Riddle resolved|journal=Nature Reports Climate Change|volume=1|date=November 2008|issue=811|pages=139|doi=10.1038/climate.2008.112|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Douglass was named a fellow of [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] in 1963<ref name="APSF">{{cite web|url=http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/?tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows&#91;action&#93;=list&tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows&#91;controller&#93;=Fellows&cHash=8f53adde7b4458aff6de5c2679773fee|title=Past Fellows|last=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|work=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Official Website|publisher=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]]|accessdate=21 October 2014|archive-date=23 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140923123354/http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/?tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows&#91;action&#93;=list&tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows&#91;controller&#93;=Fellows&cHash=8f53adde7b4458aff6de5c2679773fee|url-status=dead}}</ref> and elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1969.<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive, search on year 1969 and institution University of Chicago|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1969&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Chicago}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]].
